title: More pressure through a tube
hook: Change pressure difference and predict laminar volume-flow rate.
misconception: laminar volume-flow rate stays fixed when pressure difference doubles.
objective: Apply Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL) to compare laminar volume-flow rate when pressure difference changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With ideal Poiseuille flow with fixed radius viscosity and tube length, Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL). When pressure difference doubles, laminar volume-flow rate becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider ideal Poiseuille flow with fixed radius viscosity and tube length, with a nonzero initial result. If pressure difference triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on laminar volume-flow rate?
recall.why: Apply Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
